text:
mike_support: getting a 401 invalid_api_key for hosted API only after prod deploy. Works locally and in staging. browser console shows 401 on fetch. curl from my laptop works. any ideas?

lina_engineer: can you paste the curl you ran from prod (or the browser failing request)? quick thought: are you sure the exact same key is being used in prod env? env var / secret mismatch is common.

mike_support: here — prod pod env has REDWOOD_API_KEY set. curl from inside prod pod (kubectl exec) reproduces the 401:
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer rk_live_XXXREDACTED" -H "Origin: https://app.example.com" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/chat/completions
*   Trying 1.2.3.4...
* Connected to api.redwood.example.com (1.2.3.4) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example.com
> Authorization: Bearer rk_live_XXXREDACTED
> Origin: https://app.example.com
> 
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< content-type: application/json
< 
{"error":{"type":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key not valid for this origin or request type"}}
```

maria_support: that response string looks like an origin-bound rejection. did someone create the key with an "allowed origins" policy? that would let it work from staging origin but block prod origin.

kyle_prod: ahhh yes — we created a short-lived key during staging testing and locked it to https://staging.example.com in the dashboard. when I rotated and re-used the same label I missed the origin restriction. prod origin is https://app.example.com.

lina_engineer: yep that's the cause. origin-restricted keys are valid but the server enforces the Origin header for browser requests. server-to-server calls ignore that (or require different scope). since your curl included Origin, the check fired.

mike_support: oh thanks — so why did it work from my laptop?

kyle_prod: your laptop's curl didn't send an Origin header by default, so it bypassed the origin check. the pod/browser sets Origin automatically. you can repro locally with `-H "Origin: https://app.example.com"`.

maria_support: suggested fixes: 1) issue a non-origin-bound key for production server-side use, 2) update the key's allowed origins to include https://app.example.com (or add a production key), or 3) move fetch to server-side proxy so keys aren't in browser.

devops: quick repro command I ran in prod: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer rk_live_YYYREDACTED" -H "Origin: https://app.example.com" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/embeddings` -> same 401 with invalid_api_key. after updating allowed origins in dashboard to add https://app.example.com, requests started succeeding immediately.

mike_support: that solved it for us. updated the key to include prod origin and everything is green. thanks all. :tada:

support-bot: created ticket #S-20481 and linked to this thread for follow-up docs (we should add a note to the onboarding checklist about origin-bound keys).

lina_engineer: can we add a small note to the dashboard UI tooltip about origin-only keys causing 401s in prod? filed #DOCS-412. :thumbsup:

mike_support: closing thread — will ping if anything else crops up.
